summary.text: Nik Sandman, a retired farmer and rural mail carrier from Wauneta who ran for the Libertarian Party, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Nebraska's 1st Congressional District to Mike Flood.
He says he was a Democrat until about two years before his 2026 run.

paragraphs.text: Sandman graduated from Wauneta High School in 1967 and earned a bachelor's degree in philosophy from the University of Nebraska in 1979.
He worked as a wheat, milo and melon farmer for 26 years and as a rural mail carrier for 15 years.
He says he is a Lutheran who was converted at age 17, studied religious and philosophical thought, and served as a campus minister.
Sandman says he was a lifelong Democrat until switching to the Libertarian Party about two years before running, and he advanced from the May 12, 2026 Libertarian Party primary.
He says he is 77 and has been married to Colleen for 45 years; they have three children.
During the campaign, he said the country needs "redirection" and supported extending Medicare to all Americans and rethinking farm subsidies.
He received 1.8% of the vote to Mike Flood's 50%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
